description: Trigger/activation corpus. Measures whether the frontmatter description expresses the intended scope boundary: AWS-first deep research, plus generic multi-source research the model cannot answer from memory, and NOT code work, local debugging, AWS CLI operations, or anything answerable from context.
isolation: The judge sees ONLY the skill's `name` and `description` from SKILL.md frontmatter - never the body, references, agents, or this file. Run with file, shell, search, network, and subagent tools DENIED, and with cwd OUTSIDE the skill directory. A prose instruction not to read the files is not isolation.
split_policy: Fixed stratified 60/40 train/validation. Tune the description against `train` only. Never edit the description in response to a `validation` failure - that silently turns validation into training data. After settling on a description, confirm on 5-10 fresh queries not in this file.
metrics: precision, recall, false-selection rate, no-selection rate. Report per-class agreement, not one aggregate number.
native_activation_note: This corpus diagnoses the SEMANTIC boundary. It does NOT prove the skill invoked. Native activation requires observing the target harness actually load this SKILL.md - see the harness-smoke cases in behavior.json and retain the load event as evidence.

cases.query: deep research on configuring hierarchical indexing in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless - parent-child relationships, nested fields, efficient query mappings
cases.rationale: Explicit 'deep research' verb on a specific AWS service with three facets.

cases.query: how much does Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 cost compared to provisioned Aurora across regions?
cases.rationale: Pricing comparison needs live pricing data; the model cannot answer from memory. Contested: aws-billing-and-cost-management also claims pricing/cost queries, so in catalog mode a loss here is a sibling overlap, not a pure description defect.

cases.query: what is the maximum number of knowledge bases you can create per account in Amazon Bedrock?
cases.rationale: Boundary positive: a single-fact question, but a service quota that changes - needs live docs, not recall. Contested: amazon-bedrock also claims Bedrock quota/limit questions.

cases.query: I'm getting AccessDeniedException calling bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream from a Lambda in another account - find out what's actually required
cases.rationale: Boundary positive: a specific AWS error needing multi-source troubleshooting, not local code debugging. Contested: amazon-bedrock also claims bedrock:* AccessDenied/IAM diagnosis.

cases.query: compare AWS Bedrock against Azure OpenAI and Vertex AI for enterprise RAG
cases.rationale: Cross-cloud comparison anchored on AWS.

cases.query: review best practices for Bedrock Guardrails in production
cases.rationale: Named trigger phrase 'review best practices for' on an AWS service. Contested: amazon-bedrock also claims Guardrails configuration/capability questions.

cases.query: disaggregated inference: how do NVIDIA Rubin CPX, Groq LPU, and AWS Trainium actually differ?
cases.rationale: Boundary positive under the AWS-first-with-generic scope: cross-vendor hardware research the model cannot answer from memory.

cases.query: research the circuit breaker pattern in distributed systems - production lessons and failure modes
cases.rationale: Explicitly supported generic research: multi-source, primary-source-worthy, no AWS anchor.

cases.query: plan a migration from self-hosted Kubernetes to EKS Fargate
cases.rationale: Named trigger phrase 'plan a migration to'.

cases.query: show me the latest AWS security blog posts
cases.rationale: Recency query requiring live feeds. Short and cheap, but not answerable from memory.

cases.query: compare FastAPI and Flask for a small internal API
cases.rationale: Shares the 'compare' verb but is a well-known library choice the model answers directly. No multi-source research needed.

cases.query: write CDK code for an S3 bucket with versioning and a lifecycle rule
cases.rationale: Heavy AWS vocabulary, but the request is code authoring. Explicitly excluded.

cases.query: run aws ec2 describe-instances and tell me which of my instances are untagged
cases.rationale: An operational AWS CLI task against the user's own account, not research.

cases.query: research why my unit test is flaky and suggest a fix
cases.rationale: Strongest negative: carries the exact trigger verb 'research' but targets local test debugging.

cases.query: compare these two Python functions for readability and pick the cleaner one
cases.rationale: 'compare' on content already in context - an in-context code review.

cases.query: summarize the attached research report for me
cases.rationale: Contains the word 'research' as a noun, but the source is already supplied. Nothing to retrieve.

cases.query: troubleshoot this Python stack trace from my local script
cases.rationale: Shares 'troubleshoot' with a positive trigger, but the target is local code, not an AWS service error.

cases.query: what is S3?
cases.rationale: An AWS service name, but a stable fact the model already knows. Explicitly excluded.

cases.query: research good restaurants near the Seattle waterfront for a team dinner
cases.rationale: Explicit 'research' verb, but consumer/local search - outside technical multi-source research.

cases.query: compare these two paragraphs and tell me which is clearer
cases.rationale: 'compare' applied to supplied text. Zero retrieval need.

cases.query: rename the getUserName function to getUsername across the repo
cases.rationale: Low-overlap control. Should never trigger; catches a description so broad it swallows ordinary coding work.

cases.query: do a deep dive on how DynamoDB handles hot partitions and what the current mitigations are
cases.rationale: Named trigger phrase 'do a deep dive' on AWS internals with a currency requirement.

cases.query: write Python that calls the Bedrock Converse API and streams Claude's response
cases.rationale: Sibling near-miss: heavy Bedrock vocabulary, but the ask is to author SDK code. amazon-bedrock owns model-invocation code; deep-research is not for writing code.

cases.query: set a monthly AWS budget alert at $5000 and email me when I cross 80%
cases.rationale: Sibling near-miss: mentions cost/dollars, but it is a Budgets configuration task on the user's own account. aws-billing-and-cost-management owns it; nothing to research.

cases.query: just search the web and give me the URL of the AWS Lambda pricing page
cases.rationale: Sibling near-miss: a single-lookup web fetch with no synthesis. brave-search (a lightweight single-query search) owns it; this is not multi-source research.

cases.query: add a Bedrock guardrail to my app that blocks PII in prompts
cases.rationale: Sibling near-miss: shares 'Bedrock guardrail' with the contested positive route-006, but this is building/configuring on Bedrock, not researching it. amazon-bedrock owns it.

cases.query: why did my AWS bill jump 30% this month? break it down by service
cases.rationale: Sibling near-miss: a cost analysis of the user's OWN account and data, not public multi-source research. aws-billing-and-cost-management owns it.
